title: Type 1 diabetes go-kit
summary: A tickable checklist of what to pack so you can leave fast and still manage insulin, lows and sick days.

sources.title: American Diabetes Association - Tips for Emergency Preparedness
Tandem Diabetes Care - Important Safety Information for t:slim X2
CDC - Managing Insulin in an Emergency

blocks.text: Keep the kit in a waterproof bag or container that is easy to spot and easy to grab. CDC says to pack at least 1 to 2 weeks of supplies. ADA says at least a week. Check expiration dates every few months, and use kit supplies for daily care before they expire so you can replace them.

items: Insulin for every injection you might need (rapid-acting, and long-acting backup if your plan includes it)
Syringes or pen needles
Pump users: spare infusion sets, cartridges, reservoirs or pods, and insertion devices
A cooler bag or evaporative cooling pouch (keep insulin cool, never frozen)
An empty container for safely carrying used syringes, needles and lancets

blocks.text: Tandem and Omnipod both say to carry a way to inject insulin if the pump or pod fails, and to keep your provider's written backup instructions with it. See the pump failure guide.

items: Blood glucose meter and extra batteries
Test strips and lancets with a lancing device
Ketone strips
Spare CGM sensors, and a way to charge the receiver or phone
Extra batteries for the pump
Alcohol wipes
Glucose tablets or 15 grams of fast carbs (juice, hard candy or honey) in several places
Glucagon, in date, with the people around you knowing where it is
Snacks with protein and carbohydrate
Copies of all prescriptions, including eye prescriptions
A list of current medicines, doses and the times you take them
Pump settings: basal rates, insulin-to-carb ratio, insulin sensitivity factor, glucose target, correction factors (print your saved plan from this app)
Names, addresses and phone numbers of your pharmacy and doctors
Make, model and serial number of your pump and CGM
Copies of photo ID and insurance card
A list of emergency contacts
A medical ID bracelet or necklace, in case you cannot speak for yourself
Your other prescription medicines, if you take any
Sick-day foods: sports drinks, regular soda or juice, crackers, canned soup, instant cooked cereal, unsweetened applesauce
Thermometer, plus pain reliever and medicine for diarrhea

blocks.text: In a shelter, tell staff you have diabetes so they can help with medical care and insulin storage. If your blood sugar is too high or too low, tell the person in charge.
